problem: The rule omits the operational conditions for returning null. It can also imply that naming an object without a relevant thesis is enough to return null, although the recorded test returns the ranked list for named objects.
correct: D91 uses the absence of a named company or theme and of a text-index match; D132 adds a semantic similarity floor where semantic coverage is available. Otherwise the caller receives the ranked results and judges relevance.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1818-1819 says a named NVDA nonsense idea gets NVDA views for the caller to reject; docs/DECISIONS.md:2000 adds the 0.30 floor.

problem: The standing rule omits the specified gap before the first cited evidence and related-thesis item.
correct: Include the 12px heading-to-content gap for the first cited evidence and first related-thesis item, without extra row padding.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1831: “The first cited evidence and first related-thesis item use the same 12px heading-to-content gap as prose sections, without extra row padding.”

problem: The rule omits what happens to the height after the transition finishes.
correct: The final height returns to automatic sizing.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1855: “the final height returns to automatic sizing.”

problem: The rule omits the separate animation of expanding evidence summaries.
correct: Evidence summaries animate their own height when their text expands, in addition to the disclosure-content behavior.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1873: “Evidence summaries animate their own height when the text expands.”

problem: The rule retains the old placement after the source details but omits the later decisions that put source, type and date together in both states.
correct: Keep the quotation marks. Collapsed metadata includes source, type and full date beneath the summary; expanded metadata appends type and date to the original-source attribution, or to the publisher when there is no separate original source.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1893-1897: “Expanded evidence appends type and full date to its original-source attribution”; “Both states now use source, type and full date in the same order.”

problem: The rule omits the specified keyboard opening, navigation and selection behavior, and the opening transition.
correct: The trigger or an arrow key opens the menu; Arrow keys and Home/End move through options; Enter/Space selects; opening uses a short transition.
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md:1905-1906: “opening uses a short transition”; “Arrow keys and Home/End move through the options; Enter/Space selects.”
